explainedBy: The order is fixed: behavior is corrected first, the person is reaffirmed second.

storyboard.claim: Tough on the behavior first, nice to the person second, in that exact order.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-step flow: tough on behavior, then nice to the person.
storyboard.onScreenText: Tough on behavior, then nice to the person
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the chapter on the soft-touch manager with a structural rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: Turns the order of operations into a visible cause and effect chain.
storyboard.staging: Diagram only, no person: the order is the claim.

explainedBy: The soft-touch manager hands every employee the same perfect 10 on the review sheet.

storyboard.claim: The soft-touch manager rates everyone a perfect 10.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager picks up the review sheet and gives a perfect score.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the principle to the manager acting on it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the act itself: the sheet is the rating.
storyboard.staging: A warm, well-meaning manager reaching for the review sheet.

explainedBy: The same manager still holds the sheet and gives the failing employees the top score too.

storyboard.claim: The perfect 10 also goes to people who are objectively failing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same manager still holding the sheet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same manager and sheet; the callout widens to the failing staff.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds that the score is given regardless of performance.
storyboard.staging: Manager stays on the sheet, face neutral, the callout carries the failing.

explainedBy: The manager thinks he boosts morale while the high performer beside him is what gets hollowed out.

storyboard.claim: The manager believes he boosts morale; it actually destroys morale of high performers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager, pleased, with the sheet; a high performer enters beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; a high performer joins to be the one harmed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the cost on a person instead of on the abstract idea of morale.
storyboard.staging: Manager looks pleased (genuine intent), john stands by as the high performer.

explainedBy: The hard-working high performer sees the slacker get the identical score and bonus, so excellence loses its value.

storyboard.claim: High performers see slackers get the same score and bonus.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two men side by side, one slumped, one with the same score.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A new stage: the high performer and the slacker side by side.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the unfairness a visible comparison between two people.
storyboard.staging: John slumps worried; paul stands beside him as the one who did not earn it.

explainedBy: When a top score is guaranteed, the high performer stops trying: the unfairness is the claim.

storyboard.claim: A guaranteed 10 makes effort pointless; it is unfairness disguised as kindness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John slumped, blank, having given up effort.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows from the pair to the high performer alone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the consequence as apathy in the person.
storyboard.staging: Blank face and slump read as withdrawn effort.

explainedBy: The narrator sets up the objection that starting tough breaks the relationship.

storyboard.claim: The hosts challenge the tough-first idea.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Calm narrator presence, no face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the example to the objection.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the debate for the viewer.

explainedBy: A new hire who is corrected hard in the first week may fear the boss.

storyboard.claim: A new employee may be terrified of a boss who is tough in week one.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young new hire looks afraid beside the manager.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The objection gets a person: the new hire.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the fear on a named-role newcomer, not on an abstraction.

explainedBy: Toughness makes people defensive right away.

storyboard.claim: People get defensive instantly when you are tough.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same two people; the young employee looks worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage, face moves from afraid to worried.
storyboard.addedInformation: The word defensive is carried by the callout.

explainedBy: The objection: toughness seems to break the psychological safety HR asks for.

storyboard.claim: Tough management seems to shatter psychological safety.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same two people, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the claim moves to psychological safety.
storyboard.addedInformation: The objection is named, not yet answered.
storyboard.staging: Worried young employee beside the manager.

explainedBy: The answer: toughness only breaks safety when the goal was never clear.

storyboard.claim: Toughness only shatters safety if the toughness is arbitrary or the goal was not clear.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target icon for the goal, with the two people beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The target enters as the one-page goal that the answer depends on.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the goal as the thing that decides the outcome.
storyboard.staging: Neutral faces; the target is the shared goal.

explainedBy: An ambush with a rule nobody knew about is the case that does terrify people.

storyboard.claim: Ambushing people with an unknown rule terrifies them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The target is still there; the young employee now looks afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same goal, the face shows the bad case.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fear comes from the ambush, not from toughness itself.
storyboard.staging: Afraid young employee with the target.

explainedBy: The good case: the two sat side by side and agreed the one-page goal together.

storyboard.claim: They agreed the one-page goal together.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same target; the two are talking together.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Afraid becomes agreed: the same goal, now shared.
storyboard.addedInformation: The agreement is the foundation that prevents the fear.
storyboard.staging: Two people talking over the target.

explainedBy: Toughness on the behavior is not an attack on the person; it measures against the agreed goal.

storyboard.claim: Toughness is aimed at the behavior, not the person.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager points at the target.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the manager now points at the goal.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pointing shows where the toughness is aimed.
storyboard.staging: Manager points at the shared target.

explainedBy: The manager holds up the agreed standard, the one-page goal, as the measure.

storyboard.claim: The toughness is holding up the standard they both agreed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager holds the sheet up beside the target.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the sheet is now held up as the standard.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sheet is the standard, not the person.

explainedBy: Negation: it is not a personal attack, so the picture shows neither hatred nor anger.

storyboard.claim: It is objective toughness, not hate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Calm manager and young employee at the target.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same calm stage, the negation is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Staging stays calm so the negation is not read as hostility.

explainedBy: The objective fact: the output does not match the goal they wrote.

storyboard.claim: The output does not match the one-page goal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager points at the target while the output is compared.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the point is now the mismatch.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the comparison between output and goal concrete.

explainedBy: The second half of the redirect: the person is better than the mistake and is trusted.

storyboard.claim: The manager tells them they are better than the mistake.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager talks warmly to the young employee.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; warmth replaces the objective fact.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the reaffirmation of the person.

explainedBy: Care plus belief: the manager tells the truth because he believes they can fix it.

storyboard.claim: They see the manager cares enough to tell the truth and believes they can fix it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same warm talk at the target.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage, the belief is named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Restores the psychological safety the objection asked about.

explainedBy: The order of operations: behavior first, person second, is the rule that cannot be bent.

storyboard.claim: The order of behavior then person is non-negotiable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Calm stage with the target.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the objection with the rule; the next beat changes setting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Restates the rule as the closing claim.

explainedBy: The coach confronts a player in a championship game, so the high-stakes setting is the claim.

storyboard.claim: A championship basketball game sets the scene for the coach.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An arena with a coach and a player at the sideline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A new setting: the corporate office becomes an arena.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the lesson in a high-stakes setting.
storyboard.staging: Angry coach beside the player on the arena stage.

explainedBy: The team's best player loafs on defense while the stakes are high.

storyboard.claim: The star player is loafing on defense.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The star, blank and slumped, beside the coach.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The star becomes the subject.
storyboard.addedInformation: The blank face shows the loafing as apathy.

explainedBy: The star jogs back without trying and misses easy rebounds.

storyboard.claim: The star jogs back, not trying, missing easy rebounds.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The star walking back, blank.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the star now walks back without effort.
storyboard.addedInformation: The walk shows the not-trying.

explainedBy: The coach sits the star on the bench in public, a visible consequence.

storyboard.claim: The coach sits the star on the bench in front of the arena.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The star sits on the bench at the sideline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The walk becomes the bench.
storyboard.addedInformation: The public setting is the consequence.
storyboard.staging: Sad star seated on the bench.

explainedBy: The coach gets in the star's face and says he is angry.

storyboard.claim: The coach is aggressively tough on the behavior.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The angry coach talks at the seated star.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The coach now confronts the star.
storyboard.addedInformation: The anger is shown, not hidden.

explainedBy: The coach calls out the effort: the star does not even look like he is trying.

storyboard.claim: The star does not even look like he is trying.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The angry coach still talking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the callout names the not-trying.
storyboard.addedInformation: Keeps the tough half before the pause.

explainedBy: The second half: the coach reaffirms the star as a champion who can play better.

storyboard.claim: You are better than this; you are a champion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The coach turns warm, talking to the seated star.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Anger turns to warmth: the second half of the redirect.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reaffirmation is shown on the face.

explainedBy: The lesson for leaders: the best people cannot be allowed to play poorly.

storyboard.claim: Leaders cannot let their best people play poorly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The coach talks to the arena.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the example to the leadership lesson.
storyboard.addedInformation: Generalises the lesson from the arena to organisations.

explainedBy: Cause and effect: if the star slacks, the standard for the whole team drops.

storyboard.claim: If the star slacks without consequence, the team standard drops.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow: the star slacks off, then the standard drops.
storyboard.onScreenText: A slacking star drops the standard
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A structural cause and effect after the lesson.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the chain visible.

explainedBy: A fast, caring redirect gets even a star back on track, and the star stews in his own poor effort.

storyboard.claim: A redirect works even for a star.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The star slumped on the bench, worried, with the coach beside him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the arena after the flow.
storyboard.addedInformation: The star stews in his own effort.

explainedBy: The star gets up and goes back in, ready to play.

storyboard.claim: The star says he is ready and goes back in to win.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The star stands and walks back in.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the bench to the return.
storyboard.addedInformation: The return is the change of state.

explainedBy: The narrator names the coach's method: ruthlessly tough on loafing, supportive of potential.

storyboard.claim: The coach was ruthlessly tough on loafing and supportive of potential.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator voice, calm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the example to the summary of the method.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the method.

explainedBy: The quote: some people are disguised as losers; their look fools you.

storyboard.claim: Everyone is a potential winner; some are disguised as losers.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mask icon for the disguise, narrator voice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The quote follows the method.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask shows the disguise, a false face.

explainedBy: The coach did not call the star a loser; he pointed at the behavior.

storyboard.claim: The coach identified the loser behavior, not the person.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The coach points at the star.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same arena; the focus is the behavior.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the separation of behavior from person.

explainedBy: The objection: what if the player never gets off the bench?

storyboard.claim: What if they never get off the bench?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worried star sits on the bench.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the bench with a new worry.
storyboard.addedInformation: The worry is the bench, shown.

explainedBy: The objection continues: what if you do everything right, with the goal written together and the one-minute redirect?

storyboard.claim: What if you do everything right?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager holds the goal sheet in the office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the office with the sheet.
storyboard.addedInformation: The sheet is the goal written together.

explainedBy: The worst case: the employee sits there, pouts and refuses to change.

storyboard.claim: They sit and pout and refuse to change.
storyboard.concreteVisual: John seated, blank, refusing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The refusal is now the subject.
storyboard.addedInformation: Blank face reads as refusal.

noVisual: The book's pragmatic answer is a claim about a limit; no vocabulary item shows it.
explainedBy: The narrator answers the question: no, the book is pragmatic about this.

storyboard.claim: The book is pragmatic: one-minute redirects do not repeat forever.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator presence only.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ends the chapter on the pragmatic answer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Weak: the pragmatism is text-carried only.
